chapters.title: A machine stops: why AI needs factory context
Asset identity, constraints and data quality
Architecture with Azure, Fabric and Power BI
Semantic layer, simulation and accountable decisions

takeaways: Factory AI fails less from weak models than from missing context: which asset, operation, order, tool, person and rule an event belongs to.
A semantic layer or knowledge graph should connect facts across ERP, MES, maintenance, quality and machine data while the source systems keep ownership.
Prediction, simulation, optimization and generative AI have different jobs, and a named person still approves decisions while safety and control stay in the operational layer.
hook: A machine stops and ERP, MES, maintenance and the PLC each know part of the story, so AI cannot safely optimize the response. This episode shows manufacturing and data leaders how semantic layers, knowledge graphs, digital twins and clear constraints give AI the factory context it needs to support real production decisions.
